text:
sophie: Hey team, running into a weird onboarding quirk with the new Next.js + LangChain sample kit using the Redwood SDK — SSR requests intermittently 401 during local dev, but API routes are fine. Anyone seen this?

 tj: Can you paste the minimal repro or the auth flow you're using?

 sophie: It's the sample in /examples/next-langchain-bridge. We wire the SDK with ephemeral tokens from the dev proxy. On page load SSR fetch to /api/generate sometimes returns 401, refresh fixes it. No consistent pattern.

 alex: Sounds like a token rotation/timing race. Are you using the browser auth token to call server-side code, or exchanging it server-side?

 sophie: We exchange server-side via getServerSideProps -> fetch('/api/generate') which calls Redwood client with Authorization: Bearer <ephemeral>. Code snippet: 
```js
// pages/index.js (simplified)
export async function getServerSideProps(ctx) {
  const res = await fetch('http://localhost:3000/api/generate', { headers: { cookie: ctx.req.headers.cookie } });
  const data = await res.json();
  return { props: { data } }
}
```

 maria: If you're relying on dev-proxy cookies, sometimes the token set is async and SSR hits before it's persisted. We had a similar flake where the dev proxy sets a cookie with SameSite issues.

 sam: Can you confirm the failing response body? Is it Redwood API returning a 401 with "invalid_token" or the dev proxy gate rejecting?

 sophie: It's the Redwood hosted dev token exchange returning: `{ "error": "unauthorized", "message": "token not found" }`. Happens ~1/10 requests locally.

 tj: Two quick checks: (1) try adding a short wait in dev to see if it's a race (bad, but diagnostic). (2) log cookie header at the /api/generate entry. If cookie missing, you'll see it.

 alex: Also check if fetch from getServerSideProps is hitting same host/port env as the proxy. SSR in Next can run in a different server context when using next dev with proxying.

 sophie: Reproduced with these logs — cookie header sometimes empty. Adding a 100ms delay reduces flakes.

 maria: Ok that nails a timing race. For the sample app we should: (A) update README to recommend server-side token exchange pattern (don't call browser-only token endpoints from SSR), (B) add a guard in /api/generate that retries once if token missing (idempotent), and (C) include a small note in devx docs about cookie propagation in Next dev server.

 tj: For (B) avoid long sleeps — do an immediate retry with a short exponential backoff and log an incident if it recurs. E.g. try up to 2 attempts with 50ms jitter.

 sam: I can open a tiny PR to the example that adds the retry wrapper and a verbose dev log so users know what's happening. Want me to include a test that simulates missing cookie?

 sophie: Yes please. Also adding a one-liner in the quickstart: "If SSR occasionally returns 401 during local dev, try clearing dev proxy cookies or restart dev server" might save folks a headache.

 deploy-bot: Reminder: examples/* deploy pipeline will run once PR is opened — add --ci flag if you need to skip local dev-only flakiness in tests.

 alex: One more thought — also show an example using getInitialProps vs getServerSideProps caveats. Some users copy patterns that break when migrating to App Router.

 sophie: Great, thanks everyone. Sam, if you send the PR link I'll review and we can merge a small DX patch + README note.

 sam: On it. I'll include a tiny test harness that toggles cookie presence to assert retry behavior.

 tj: Thanks, this will reduce onboarding friction a lot. :thumbsup:
